balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

treasury.title: Cash and treasury investments
treasury.content:
Cash only is bank balances and equivalents; short-term investments are treasury products maturing within a year; long-term treasury investments are the same kind of instrument held beyond a year, reported separately on the balance sheet.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: the three lines together, not cash alone, are the liquidity management actually controls -- Tuhu parks a large share of its net-cash position in short- and long-term wealth-management products rather than bank deposits.

What to watch:

  • Long-term treasury balances growing while cash-only shrinks (duration extension for yield)
  • Total of the three versus total debt, for the real net-cash position

storeNetwork.title: Self-operated vs franchised workshop network
storeNetwork.content:
Self-operated stores are Tuhu-run outlets; franchised workshops are independently owned garages operating under the Tuhu Workshop brand and supplied through Tuhu's platform.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: franchised workshops are the much larger and faster-growing part of the network (7,833 vs 175 self-operated stores at FY2025) -- the business scales its physical footprint mostly through asset-light franchising, not capital-intensive company-owned stores.

What to watch:

  • Franchise count growth relative to self-operated stores (capital intensity of expansion)
  • Franchise closures or churn, which the net count alone can hide

userFunnel.title: Registered users vs active customers
userFunnel.content:
Registered users are everyone who has created a Tuhu account; active customers are the subset who actually transacted in the period (TTM for interim rows). The ratio between them is the activation rate.

For Tuhu Car Inc.: registered users have grown from 95.5m (FY2022) to 162.3m (FY2025) while active customers grew from 16.5m to 28.4m over the same span -- activation sits around 17-18%, so the bulk of the registered base is not yet a transacting customer, which is either runway or a monetisation problem depending on the trend.

What to watch:

  • Activation % rising (existing base converting) versus falling (growth driven only by new sign-ups)
  • Active customer growth rate relative to registered-user growth rate
